subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord support guild-scoped trusted inbound webhook IDs that bypass the default bot-message drop, and may those webhook messages map onto a configured user identity?
rationale: The allowlist is narrower than `allowBots: true`, but it adds a new inbound trust surface and the proposed user mapping can affect authorization, routing, and session identity.

options.title: Allow Webhooks Without User Mapping
options.body: Permit selected Discord webhook IDs to pass the bot-message gate while keeping sender identity as the webhook or bot identity until the identity contract is separately approved.

options.title: Allow Webhook-To-Principal Mapping
options.body: Permit mapping only through a maintainer-approved stable identity-link contract with validation, audit behavior, and tests proving it cannot bypass sender authorization or session isolation.

options.title: Decline Discord-Native Trusted Ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automation to generic hooks or a separate plugin/API design instead of adding this channel trust surface.

recommendation.title: Allow Webhooks Without User Mapping
recommendation.body: Permit selected Discord webhook IDs to pass the bot-message gate while keeping sender identity as the webhook or bot identity until the identity contract is separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible routing signal for the security/product decision and adjacent Discord policy history, while implementation ownership is shared.
